picks.name: The Pet Parent
picks.why_plausible: Treats the pet as family, reads ingredient labels and pays a premium for health — exactly the senior-dog joint-health buyer. Affinities include pet_food, pet_health and subscription_boxes with price_sensitivity low-medium and AOV $72, matching the $75 first order.
lean_into: emotional connection: more good years with your dog
picks.ad_angle: Emotional longevity: the food that helps your aging best friend keep up, formulated by vets with ingredients you can read.

picks.name: The Busy Parent
picks.why_plausible: Has pet_food in affinities, 'loves subscriptions' and is convenience-motivated, so auto-delivery of the right senior formula fits a time-poor household. Price sensitivity medium but typical AOV $78 covers the first order.
lean_into: time-saving: the right food shows up automatically
trusted, no-guesswork formula for an older dog
family-friendly — the dog is part of the family too
avoid: complicated onboarding or long science explanations
picks.ad_angle: One less thing to remember: senior-dog nutrition on autopilot, delivered before you run out.

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: Pays premiums for evidence-backed products and wants science-backed claims and ingredient transparency — a natural fit for a vet-formulated joint-health formula, applied to her dog. price_sensitivity: low, AOV $95.
picks.ad_angle: Optimize your dog's healthspan: the same evidence-first standard you use for yourself, in his bowl.

picks.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
picks.why_plausible: Heavy subscription user who defaults to whatever is frictionless; the brand is subscription-only replenishment, which matches rather than annoys him. Mid-to-high income, medium price sensitivity, AOV $55 is a modest stretch.
lean_into: one-click start, skip or pause anytime
no more last-minute pet store runs
picks.ad_angle: Frictionless resupply: pick your dog's size, click once, and premium senior food arrives on schedule forever.

plan.summary: The two best pet audiences are direct pet-food competitors, so the plan rests on a capped Tailcrate pet test plus clean-ingredient grocery and science-forward wellness audiences that match on values and spending power but carry no pet-ownership signal.

test.name: Pantrygood
test.rationale: Pantrygood's notes describe shoppers 'Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims' at a high income tier and $86 typical order, so grain-free and vet-formulated claims land and the $75 price is unremarkable to them.

evidence.quote: Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims

test.risk: No pet-ownership signal at all — you're paying for reach where a large share of impressions have no dog, let alone a senior one.

test.name: Tailcrate
test.adjustment_reason: Notes say the audience is 'Millennials treating dogs as family' with a '25-45' age skew and that a 'Fun, playful brand voice converts best' — both the likely dog life-stage and the required tone work against a vet-formulated senior-dog subscription.
test.rationale: Tailcrate is the only reachable pet audience, and dog-owner intent plus a $35 basket means a $75 premium food offer is a real stretch but worth a contained test. The playful, younger-dog framing is the opposite of the clinical joint-health message this brand leads with.

evidence.quote: Millennials treating dogs as family. Fun, playful brand voice converts best

test.risk: Younger owners with younger dogs are simply out of market for senior formula, and a treats/toys box makes it a partial substitute, so conversion may be thin at 2.1× the typical order.

test.name: Daily Form
test.rationale: Daily Form's 'Science-forward wellness' audience is the rare group that rewards a vet-formulated, longevity claim, and the subscription-supplement habit mirrors your replenishment model.

evidence.quote: Science-forward wellness. Audience skeptical of unsubstantiated health claims

test.risk: That same audience is 'skeptical of unsubstantiated health claims', so joint-health and longevity copy needs visible vet/evidence backing; the 22-42 skew also sits below your 35-65 target.

campaign.name: Premium grain-free, vet-formulated dog food for senior dogs, sold on subscription · post-purchase launch

bid_strategy.rationale: $75 first order (assumed) × 0.60 = $45.00 target CPA: subscription revenue repeats, so a first order can be bought at a larger share of its value. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: We assumed a first order of about $75, typical for premium dog food subscriptions.
We assumed the audience is any gender, skewing 35-65.
We treated the product as subscription-only since only a subscription is mentioned.
Allowable CPA is 60% of first order value (subscription); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so the whole budget is a test. Treat results as exploratory.
Target CPA is based on an assumed order value. Confirm price before launch.
